inventory.anchor: WebrtcTCPSocket::OpenWithoutHttpProxy (after the local address is parsed, before mTransport->Bind)
inventory.notes: Before the bind of a plain TCP socket of a PeerConnection, StealthTcpSocketBorn gives the socket's transport the context of its name lookup and makes the bind address the wildcard of the declared address's family on port 0.

The responder sets the multicast interface to the address it joined on, or a query would leave on the default multicast route and never come back to its socket (on Linux a join on the loopback hears nothing without it). The loop iterates by reference so the first address stays available.

inventory.anchor: include of nr_stealth_network.h; NrSocket::create (after the address is converted, the bind failure, the declared address kept, the attach to the socket transport service); NrSocket::sendto; NrSocket::recvfrom; NrSocket::close
inventory.notes: The host UDP socket of a declared address: it binds the wildcard of the address's family on the candidate's port, keeps the declared address (with that port) as its own, and records the port in the set of this process's own ports until close. A datagram to another socket of this process goes on the kernel's loopback (sendto and recvfrom rewrite the peer address), a bind refused for a port in use or not allowed answers R_ALREADY so ICE takes the next port, and a test switch can refuse the attach.

inventory.anchor: class NrSocket (private members, after the friend of StealthNrSocketAccess)
inventory.notes: Member stealth_own_port_: the port this socket recorded in the set of this process's own ports (0 when none). StealthSocketAttached sets it and StealthOwnPortReleased clears it at close.

inventory.anchor: include of RandomNum.h; NrIceCtx constructor (host_ports_); nr_socket_local_create
inventory.notes: A host UDP socket of a declared address takes the next port of its connection; a busy port (R_ALREADY from NrSocket::create) is skipped, as the kernel skips it. Loopback and wildcard addresses go the plain way. The loop of 64 tries is the one piece of logic here; it could move behind one call.

inventory.anchor: include of nr_stealth_network.h; nr_ice_get_default_local_address; nr_ice_set_local_addresses (no default address)
inventory.notes: The default address of a family is the declared entry of that family (nr_stealth_default_local_address): the route probe (a UDP socket connected to the page's server or a public address, then getsockname) is gone, with it the wildcard refusal and the fallback to every filtered address. A family the declaration does not have has no default address, as a machine with no route in that family. Mozilla's probing function is replaced by one call.
